verse.text: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away.

reflection.observation: In a chapter where Jesus speaks about the end times, wars, famines, and cosmic upheaval, He anchors everything with this promise. The temporary nature of our physical world — even something as vast as 'heaven and earth' — is contrasted with the permanence of His words. This isn't about the Bible as a book; it's about the reliability of everything Jesus has spoken. When everything feels unstable, His promises remain.
reflection.application: What are you anchoring your life to that is actually temporary? A job, a relationship, a political outcome, your health, financial security — all of these can shift overnight. Today, identify one area where you've been treating something temporary as permanent. Write down one specific promise from Scripture that you can anchor to instead. Make it visible somewhere you'll see it this week.
reflection.prayer: Lord, I confess that I often build my security on things that are passing away — my plans, my possessions, my reputation. Your Word is the only bedrock that never shifts. Help me to treasure Your promises above every temporary thing. When anxiety comes, remind me that Your words outlast heaven and earth themselves. I anchor my soul in You today. Amen.
